retraction.reason: Re-read on 24 September under A14(6) against the bar that replaced M44b’s: a record earns its place by carrying at least one honest edge to anything already in the atlas, and nobody invents an edge to save a record. The corpus is now 859 active events across all five lanes. M44b judged this record against the Portuguese core alone. South America is in the atlas now, with 47 active events, which is what M44b said was missing. The article, at revision 1370610658, attributes the war to "a long-standing territorial dispute and to the discovery of oil deposits on the eastern Andes range" and to Standard Oil and Royal Dutch Shell. It names no event this atlas holds. The Great Depression, which the atlas does hold, is absent from its account of the origins. It is a good record that still reaches nothing. What it wants now is a Bolivian or Paraguayan neighbour, and no longer a Portuguese one.

title: Chaco War
summary: Wikidata item Q223126, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "war between Bolivia and Paraguay". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
regionNote: The Wikidata import wrote this lane, working it out from the event's own point. The event points at no place record, so the timeline has nothing else to go on.
